extra.message: When SECRET_KEY is unset, JWT signing and verification use the publicly known 'local-dev-change-me' key. An attacker can forge an HS256 token with an existing administrator's user ID and authenticate as that administrator; current_user trusts the signed sub claim.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Unauthenticated registration accepts any existing customer_id and attaches the new active user to that customer without an invitation or ownership verification. An attacker can register against another customer ID, log in, and access that customer's jobs, messages, contact information, and customer-visible proofs through the normal ownership filters.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: GET /api/export/routes loads every route and filters only dispatcher accounts. Field workers are permitted to call this endpoint but receive other workers' routes across all regions, including schedules, worker names, job references, and statuses. Unlike list_routes, this branch never checks Route.worker_id against the requesting worker.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: Job imports resolve customer and location independently and never verify location.customer_id == customer.id, although create_job explicitly requires this. A dispatcher can associate one customer's location with another customer's job. Customer portal authorization subsequently uses Job.customer_id and exposes the unrelated location through job_to_dict, breaking customer isolation.

cwe: CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

extra.message: The authentication cookie is always issued with secure=False, including when the application is served over HTTPS. Browsers may transmit this reusable session JWT over HTTP, exposing it to network interception.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Password reset updates the password and consumes the reset token without invalidating existing session JWTs. current_user checks only token validity and account activity, so a previously stolen JWT remains usable after recovery until its original expiration, normally 12 hours. Logout similarly only deletes the browser cookie at line 277 and leaves copied tokens valid.

cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: The public login endpoint performs password verification on every attempt without account-based throttling, an attempt counter, or lockout. No application middleware supplies these controls. Attackers can repeatedly guess passwords or perform credential stuffing against existing accounts.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Proof uploads are read completely into memory before the 10 MB limit is checked. An authenticated worker with an assigned job can submit an oversized file and force its entire allocation before rejection, exhausting worker memory.

cwe: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: CSV import reads and decodes the entire uploaded file, then processes every row without a file-size or row-count limit. A dispatcher can exhaust memory with a large upload or monopolize the async worker through unbounded synchronous parsing and ORM object creation.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Operational CSV exports write user-controlled values without neutralizing spreadsheet formula prefixes. A field worker can place a formula in an incident summary or internal note, which reaches the incidents export at line 863. Spreadsheet software can evaluate the formula when another user opens the report; CSV quoting does not prevent formula execution.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: The packet_ref query parameter is joined directly to BASE_EXPORT_DIR and read without containment validation. A caller with a valid x-internal-token can use ../ segments or an absolute path to read arbitrary process-readable text files. This GET route is reachable in API-only mode, when the earlier SPA catch-all is absent.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The url query parameter reaches urllib.request.urlopen without scheme, host, address, or redirect restrictions, and response content is returned. In API-only mode, a caller with a valid x-internal-token can access internal services or use file:// URLs to disclose local file contents.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: The lane query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse, allowing absolute external destinations instead of restricting redirects to application paths. In API-only mode, requests carrying a valid x-internal-token can make the trusted application redirect clients to an attacker-controlled site.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The operations tally endpoint logs the complete Authorization header and request body at WARNING level. Requests passing the internal-token gate that also carry a bearer credential expose that reusable credential and potentially sensitive payload data to log readers and log collection systems.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The expr query parameter is evaluated as Python code. Clearing __builtins__ does not sandbox Python: expressions can traverse object classes and loaded function globals to recover execution capabilities. In API-only mode, a caller with a valid x-internal-token can execute code with application privileges.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: The count query parameter directly controls an unbounded list allocation inside an async handler. In API-only mode, a caller with a valid x-internal-token can request an enormous count, exhausting memory and blocking the event loop. The nonce endpoint similarly accepts an unbounded length for synchronous string generation at line 121.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The card query parameter is explicitly marked safe in a Jinja template and returned as HTML. Arbitrary script elements or event handlers are therefore preserved and execute if a browser renders the response. Exploitation requires Jinja2 to be installed, API-only routing, and a request passing the x-internal-token gate.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The fragment query parameter is concatenated into Jinja template source and rendered with an unrestricted Template environment. Malicious template expressions can access Python objects and execute operating-system commands. Exploitation requires Jinja2 to be installed, API-only routing, and a valid x-internal-token.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The name query parameter directly determines the destination for attacker-controlled request bytes. Absolute paths and ../ segments escape BASE_EXPORT_DIR; parent directories are created and existing files are overwritten. A caller with a valid x-internal-token can create or overwrite arbitrary files permitted by the application account.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Attacker-supplied XML is parsed with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. When lxml is installed, a caller passing the internal-token gate can cause external DTD and entity resources to be resolved, including local files and network resources supported by the underlying parser. Returning only doc.tag does not prevent resource access during parsing.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The request JSON filter is passed unchanged to MongoDB find_one, with no schema or operator restrictions. When PyMongo and MongoDB are available, a caller with a valid x-internal-token can inject query operators such as $ne or $regex to select arbitrary matching records; the endpoint returns part of the selected document.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
